issues.description: The phrase 'for the food' is vague, and the Vietnamese 'bữa ăn' makes it sound like 'meal' rather than 'food'. I can follow, but the English line feels unfinished.
issues.suggested_fix: Change the line to: 'I have to buy a vegetable for the food we will make.' Vietnamese: 'Mình phải mua một loại rau cho món ăn mình sẽ làm.'

issues.description: 'Bạn không cần phải đâu' sounds a little direct and incomplete in Vietnamese. It would feel more natural if the omitted action was clear.
issues.suggested_fix: Change English to: 'You don't have to buy any. I have vegetables in the kitchen.' Vietnamese: 'Bạn không cần phải mua đâu. Mình có rau trong bếp rồi.'

issues.description: The grammar note is clear but very short. For A2, adding the verb pattern and one example would help me use it.
issues.suggested_fix: Use: 'Use have to + verb to say something is necessary. Use don't have to + verb to say something is not necessary. Example: I have to buy vegetables. You don't have to buy vegetables.'

qa_report.summary: The clip is short and clear enough for me as an A2 listener, and it uses the target word, review words, and grammar point. The main small problems are the vague 'for the food' line and the slightly machine-like Vietnamese reply. With the suggested edits, it would feel more natural and easier to learn from.
